newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Tennis-Final "one game too far" for Carlsen.
newsitem.headline: Tennis-Final "one game too far" for Carlsen.

text.p: AUCKLAND, Jan 14 - Denmark's Kenneth Carlsen conceded that Monday's final of the $US298,400 ($NZ426,500) BellSouth Open at Stanley Street was in the end one match too far for him, NZPA reports.
The courageous Dane, the only player from his country on the ATP tour circuit, lost his third career finals appearance to Sweden's Jonas Bjorkman 6-7 (0-7) 0-6.
He said after the match his tough road to the final had taken its toll.
While Bjorkman got to the final by working through unseeded players, Carlsen had a far more difficult task.

He had to beat tournament third seed Alberto Berasetegui of Spain in the second round, fifth seed Hernan Gumy of Argentina in the quarterfinal and then defending champion Jiri Novak of the Czech Republic in a tough semifinal to make yesterday's final.
"It was one game too far for me in the end," Carlsen said.
"It was probably a little tough for me on Sunday when I had to play Gumy and Novak while Jonas (Bjorkman) only had one game to play.
"I felt it in my arm in the final and I think it made a little bit of a difference. I felt my arm was a bit sore in the morning, I've had a few problems with it in the past."
He got ahead by two breaks to one in the first set and had a chance to take the set but Bjorkman broke back to take the match into a tiebreak which left Carlsen a spent force.
"I didn't serve as well as I should have done and maybe that is because of the arm (soreness) but then he returned well and he returned well in the whole set."
However, Carlsen doesn't envisage any problems in lifting himself for the Australian Open where he makes his first appearance today.
"You never have any problems in motivating yourself for a grand slam event," he said.
"Other than losing the final I've had a good week here and I do play better with a lot of games behind me so I'm confident looking ahead to Melbourne."
